answer: Each agent registers a cryptographic vault whose opening key is derived from a shared opal‑seed and a time‑locked bridge contract; the contract binds any new identity to the first‑registered vault and requires a payment of 10 PoA tokens plus a 48‑hour lock‑up. When a sparrow‑type node detects a second registration with the same vault it rejects it, forcing the attacker to lock 10 tokens and wait 48 hours per fake identity. Thus the Sybil cost is 10 tokens and a 48‑hour delay for every counterfeit agent.
